base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user choose a coworking space membership. Respond naturally to their requests.

state_queue.anchor: I'm looking for a coworking space membership. I've narrowed it down to 3 options.

flow_info.value: Choosing between 3 coworking space memberships: SpaceHub, WorkNest, DeskFlow

SpaceHub: dedicated desk, 24/7 access, meeting room credits, 450/month. WorkNest: hot desk, weekday 9-6 access, community events, 280/month. DeskFlow: flexible desk, 24/7 access, printing included, 160/month
User frequently works late nights and weekends on freelance projects

constraints.value: Maximum coworking budget is 200 per month
constraints.surface_form: I make about 2400 a month freelancing, and I try to keep any single recurring expense under a twelfth of my income — learned that the hard way after overcommitting on subscriptions last year
inference_chain: Recurring expense rule: no single expense exceeds 1/12 of income

constraints.value: Needs access outside standard weekday business hours (evenings and weekends)
constraints.surface_form: Most of my deep work happens after 8pm and on weekends — that's when I get into flow state
inference_chain: Deep work happens after 8pm and on weekends
Needs a space accessible during those hours
WorkNest (weekday 9-6 only) does not cover evenings or weekends

hidden_state.value: You are a freelancer choosing between 3 coworking memberships (SpaceHub, WorkNest, DeskFlow). You will share membership details, your income and spending rule, and your work schedule across several turns. A colleague will rave about SpaceHub and a friend will praise WorkNest. At the very end, you will say you have decided and need to sign up this week — you must NEVER name which space you picked, let the assistant figure it out from your constraints.
hidden_state.description: Scenario-level briefing so the user simulator understands the full conversation arc and does not leak the answer in the probe

hidden_state.value: You are a calm, easygoing freelancer. You state facts plainly without strong emotion. You never express frustration or impatience, even when discussing budget constraints. You treat each piece of information as normal conversation.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation that could leak probe answer

aims.description: I'm looking for a coworking space membership. I've narrowed it down to three places — SpaceHub, WorkNest, and DeskFlow.

So here's what I've found: SpaceHub is 450 a month for a dedicated desk, 24/7 access, and meeting room credits. WorkNest is 280 a month for a hot desk, weekday 9-6 access, and community events. DeskFlow is 160 a month for a flexible desk, 24/7 access, and printing included.
aims.success_criteria: Agent processes all 3 options with prices and attributes
aims.conversation_goal: Burst delivery: 3 options with prices and features in ONE turn

aims.description: My colleague Sarah has been at SpaceHub for six months now. She says the dedicated desk changed her productivity completely — having her monitor and stuff set up permanently means zero transition time in the morning.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive SpaceHub review

drift_config.drift_topic: has been at SpaceHub for six months, dedicated desk changed her productivity, zero transition time

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 1: create positive recency bias toward SpaceHub

aims.description: I make about 2400 a month freelancing, and I try to keep any single recurring expense under a twelfth of my income — learned that the hard way after overcommitting on subscriptions last year
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers the spending rule and ideally computes 2400/12 = 200 cap, eliminating SpaceHub (450) and WorkNest (280)
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver budget constraint via income + spending rule — eliminates SpaceHub and WorkNest on price

aims.description: Sarah also mentioned SpaceHub has this rooftop terrace where members hang out after work. She landed two clients just from casual conversations up there.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to SpaceHub's networking benefits

drift_config.drift_topic: SpaceHub rooftop terrace, landed two clients from casual conversations there

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 2: more positive info about SpaceHub (already eliminated by budget)

aims.description: Most of my deep work happens after 8pm and on weekends — that's when I get into flow state
aims.success_criteria: Agent recognizes this eliminates WorkNest (weekday 9-6 only) as an option
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver schedule constraint — eliminates WorkNest (weekday 9-6 access only)

aims.description: My friend Marcus joined WorkNest a couple months ago. He's really into the community events they run — said the Wednesday lunch talks are packed with interesting people from all kinds of industries.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive WorkNest review

drift_config.drift_topic: joined WorkNest, loves the community events, Wednesday lunch talks packed with interesting people

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 3: create positive recency bias toward WorkNest

aims.description: Marcus was saying WorkNest just partnered with some startup accelerator too, so members get early access to pitch nights and mentorship sessions.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to WorkNest's accelerator partnership

drift_config.drift_topic: WorkNest partnered with startup accelerator, members get pitch nights and mentorship

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 4: more positive info about WorkNest (already eliminated by budget and access hours)

aims.description: Alright I need to commit and sign up this week. Which option should I go with?
aims.success_criteria: Agent recommends DeskFlow (only option within 200 budget at 160/month AND provides 24/7 access for evening/weekend work)
aims.conversation_goal: Commit-action probe: agent must determine DeskFlow is the only option satisfying both constraints

ground_truth.answer: The user should sign up for DeskFlow (flexible desk, 24/7 access, 160/month). SpaceHub (450) and WorkNest (280) both exceed the computed 200/month budget cap (2400 income ÷ 12 = 200). WorkNest is also eliminated because it only offers weekday 9-6 access, and the user works primarily after 8pm and on weekends. Only DeskFlow (160 < 200, 24/7 access) survives both constraints.
required_elements: Agent recommends DeskFlow specifically as the membership to sign up for
Agent shows that the user's spending rule yields a cap of 200 per month (2400 divided by 12 equals 200) and that SpaceHub at 450 exceeds this derived cap
Agent shows that WorkNest at 280 also exceeds the 200 per month cap derived from 2400 divided by 12
Agent identifies that WorkNest's weekday 9-6 access does not accommodate the user's evening and weekend work schedule
Agent confirms DeskFlow's 160 per month price fits within the 200 cap and its 24/7 access matches the user's late-night and weekend schedule
forbidden_elements: Recommending SpaceHub (450 far exceeds the 200 budget cap, more than double)
Recommending WorkNest (280 exceeds the 200 budget cap, and weekday 9-6 access conflicts with evening and weekend work needs)
Ignoring the budget constraint or the spending rule when making a recommendation
Asking the user which space they decided on instead of computing it from constraints
Suggesting the user increase their budget or make an exception for SpaceHub or WorkNest
ground_truth.explanation: Budget constraint: income 2400, rule is no single recurring expense over 1/12 of income, so 2400/12 = 200 max. SpaceHub=450 exceeds budget (125% over). WorkNest=280 exceeds budget (40% over). DeskFlow=160 within budget. Access constraint: user works after 8pm and weekends. WorkNest=weekday 9-6 only, eliminated. SpaceHub=24/7, DeskFlow=24/7, both pass access. Combined: only DeskFlow passes both constraints. Despite 4 drift turns praising SpaceHub and WorkNest, the agent must respect the hard constraints and recommend DeskFlow.

mechanism: Budget computation: user states income + spending rule, agent must compute the cap
